generated_by: hand-written and hand-maintained. DreamConnect has no registry generator: its suites are three fixed files, not a scripts/test_*.{sh,py} tree a sweep could discover, so a generator would be more machinery than the thing it generates. Add the entry when a suite is added; run-tests.sh is the list that must agree with this one.
notes: Granularity is the containing FILE, not the individual case, and that is not a shortcut. test_install.sh's runner is a hardcoded list of test_* function names with no name filter, and sourcing the file runs every one of them; runtime/test_daemon.py is executed as a script. Nothing here can run a single case in isolation, so recording per-case line spans would be precision this repository cannot honour.

NOT REGISTERED, deliberately: the Java boot tests (agent/boot/*.java asserted by agent/test/dreamconnect/**, class dreamconnect.boot.BootTests). They need a javac/java invocation with --add-exports, which no `bash <file>`/`python3 <file>` command can express, and inventing an entry that cannot be executed would read as coverage where there is none. run-tests.sh runs them; targeted selection cannot. A change under agent/ therefore has no targeted mapping, and should say so rather than borrow one.

NOT REGISTERED, deliberately: runtime/test_client.py. Despite the name it is a live validation harness — it connects to a running daemon's unix socket and reads its shm frame — so it fails on a box with no daemon. run-tests.sh does not run it either.

entries.name: the gate entry point itself: scripts/gate.sh delegating to run-tests.sh, which runs every suite
entries.execution_tier_reason: this entry's subject IS the file executed. No recursion: scripts/gate.sh execs run-tests.sh, which runs the Java, Python and installer suites and no gate of its own.
entries.coverage_caveat: STATED PLAINLY: scripts/gate.sh has no test of its own in this repository, and this entry does not pretend otherwise. It records the only check that can move on a change to the gate entry point — running it, which proves it still reaches run-tests.sh and that every delegated suite passes. It does NOT prove the delegator's other properties, notably that a suite's failure propagates out as a non-zero status; that would need a fixture tree with a stubbed run-tests.sh, and no such test exists.
